messages:
incident-bot: Paging: elevated 5xx on eu-edge-frontend — alert threshold breached for handshake failures and gateway errors. Auto-escalation to #incidents. Severity: high-ish; root suspected: TLS chain issues.

sara_ops: I can confirm spike in 502/523 from eu-edge starting ~10:02 UTC. Error rate ~11% of total egress. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/2156789123

jay_oncall: pulling logs now. @matt_infra can you check cert rotator / CA chain for eu-edge? I see a lot of "tlsv1 alert unknown ca" and "handshake failure" in proxy logs.

matt_infra: running quick check against one of the edge hosts:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect edge-eu-1.redwood.ai:443 -servername edge-eu.redwood.ai -showcerts 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -text | grep -E "Issuer:|Not After"
Issuer: CN=InterCA Ltd Intermediate CA
Not After : Nov 01 07:59:59 2025 GMT
```
Chain looks like it contains an intermediate that expired yesterday (UTC). We're seeing clients rejecting chain -> handshake fails.

ana_support: customers hitting errors: acme-inc (10% of their requests), dataportal, and several smaller orgs in EU region. Support already opened priority tickets. ETA for major customer impact: 15-30 mins if not mitigated.

kevin_se: yeah this looks like a rotated root->intermediate mismatch. Rotator job tried to upload new intermediate last night but appears the intermediate on the edge fleet didn't pick up. Need to check the rotator run and the CDN sync.

jay_oncall: mitigation plan options:
- traffic-steer EU -> eu-edge-fallback pool (no expired intermediate) (fast)
- force restart edge proxy to reload cert chain from control-plane (medium risk)
- emergency uplink of a fallback cert (self-signed/short-lived) to get traffic flowing while we fix rotator (works but needs SEC ok)

sara_ops: I'm going to shift routing for a small % first (5%) to validate fallback. If stable, ramp to 100% for affected prefixes. Doing safe canary via traffic-controller now.

[system]: traffic-controller: started canary shift 5% of eu-edge incoming to eu-edge-fallback-1 for prefixes: /v1/generate,/v1/chat.

matt_infra: canary looks clean so far (5m). No handshake errors on fallback. I'm running the rotator check:
```
$ curl -sS https://rotator.redwood.ai/api/v1/status?job=intermediate-sync-eu | jq -r '.last_run, .status'
"2025-10-31T23:14:52Z"
"failed: upload error -> 403 KMS access denied"
```
Looks like the upload failed due to KMS permission issue. That would explain why new intermediate didn't propagate.

kevin_se: okay that matches incident timeline. Rotator failed last night -> intermediate expired -> edge kept serving older chain. KMS denied because of IAM policy change in the eu account during a deploy window.

jay_oncall: immediate actions:
1) ramp canary -> 50% now. (sara_ops)
2) rollback IAM change to allow rotator write to bucket (matt_infra working with sec) OR manually upload cert to fallback pool (matt).
3) open emergency support ticket with KMS team to reenable rotator (kevin).
4) notify SRE/SEC and CS (ana_support) — include affected customer list.

sara_ops: ramping to 50% now. Watching latency and 5xx.

[system]: traffic-controller: updated canary -> 50% traffic shifted to eu-edge-fallback-1.

ana_support: I sent customer comms to acme-inc and dataportal support contacts. Included workaround (retry + using eu-west backplane) and note that we're routing their traffic to fallback.

matt_infra: manual upload started to eu-edge-fallback shards with the verified intermediate cert chain (short path):
```
$ gsutil cp intermediate.pem gs://edge-cert-sync/eu/manual/2156789123-intermediate.pem
$ /opt/edge/bin/ctl apply-cert --shard eu-edge-1 --chain gs://edge-cert-sync/eu/manual/2156789123-intermediate.pem
```
Manual apply succeeded on eu-edge-fallback-1 and 2. I'm running reloads on main fleet but will wait for KMS perms to be restored for proper rotator.

kevin_se: KMS team acknowledged and reverting IAM change now; ETA 7 minutes. Rotator should be able to push the correct chain after that.

jay_oncall: once rotator confirmed, we should retract traffic-steer back to primary fleet and then restart proxies rolling to pick new chain (graceful reload). Plan: retract -> let primary serve -> do 5-host rolling reload for minimal impact.

sara_ops: 50% canary stable for 8m; 5xx rate on canary ~0.3% vs 11% on primary. Ramping to 100% for affected prefixes.

[system]: traffic-controller: completed shift -> 100% of impacted prefixes served by eu-edge-fallback-1/2/3.

matt_infra: rotator upload succeeded:
```
$ curl -sS https://rotator.redwood.ai/api/v1/runs/last?job=intermediate-sync-eu | jq -r '.result'
"success"
```
Triggering controlled rollout of correct chain to primary fleet via rotator.

kevin_se: rotator confirmed push to primary. I'll watch certificate TTL and OCSP.

jay_oncall: starting rolling reload of primary eu-edge fleet (graceful reload, 10 hosts at a time). If anything spikes, we will shift traffic back to fallback.

matt_infra: 30% hosts reloaded, chains verified with openssl. No handshake failures reported so far.

ana_support: CS updated customers with ETA ~20m for full resolution. No new escalation requests.

sara_ops: rolling reload complete. Re-checking metrics. 5xx back to baseline (<1%). Latency normal.

[system]: traffic-controller: retracting fallback route -> returning traffic to primary fleet.

jay_oncall: confirming final state: cert chain updated across fleet, rotator healthy, KMS perms restored. Closing immediate paging but leaving channel open for postmortem and timeline.

matt_infra: proposed follow-ups:
- postmortem (attach rotator logs, IAM diff)
- add rotator write retry/backoff + alert when KMS upload fails for >1h
- validate cert chain expiry detection alerting (we only alerted after errors)
- run org-wide IAM audits for deploy windows

kevin_se: SEC to review emergency manual upload and approve short-lived exception we used.

ana_support: tagging for follow-up: #postmortems, #eng-sre, #eng-security, #customer-success.

jay_oncall: handing off to night oncall @matt_infra (takes over at 00:10 UTC). I'll leave notes in the incident tracker. If anything regresses, page me again.

matt_infra: acknowledged — I'll keep a 30m watch and follow through on the postmortem items.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved: 5xx spike mitigated and traffic normalized. Severity: S2 -> under postmortem review.

sara_ops: thanks everyone. great coordination. Closing thread in 30m after doc updates.
